text:
The macroeconomic backdrop this quarter remains one of transition rather than retreat. Headline inflation has settled at 3.8%, and the policy rate now sits at 5.25% — a level the market has largely absorbed into its planning assumptions, even as high-yield spreads at 640bps signal that credit investors continue to price caution into every incremental dollar of risk. We view this as a market recalibrating, not deteriorating, and we continue to manage the portfolio accordingly.

Turning to performance: our flagship reported a return of -2.0% for the quarter, bringing the year-to-date figure to -3.5%. Since inception, the fund remains firmly positive at +18.0%, a reminder that quarterly noise should be read in the context of a multi-year value-creation program, not the reverse. Public equities were down -3.0% over the same period, and our own marks — reflected in a NAV index of 96.5 — continue to track a portfolio of businesses we know intimately, underwritten with operational discipline long before turns of leverage became a market talking point. We stand behind our marking process; it reflects real cash flow performance at the asset level, not sentiment.

We would characterize the pressure visible in select positions as temporary dislocation — a function of financing costs working through capital structures rather than any erosion in the underlying competitive position of our companies. Our operating teams, working alongside portfolio management, have spent the quarter tightening working capital cycles and re-underwriting vendor contracts across the mid-market book. This is unglamorous work, and it rarely makes headlines, but it is the work that compounds.

Looking ahead, we remain constructive, though prudently so. Should financing costs remain elevated for longer than the market currently expects, we would expect further near-term pressure on reported returns across the vintage; we are positioning the portfolio — and our conversations with lenders — with that risk firmly in view. Our engagement with long-term partners continues to reinforce our conviction that patient capital, deployed into operationally sound businesses, is best positioned to navigate this environment. We believe recovery may occur as rate conditions normalize, though the timing of that normalization remains a watch item rather than a certainty.

We thank our limited partners for their continued partnership and are, as always, available to discuss the portfolio in greater depth.

Onward.
